newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada Feb weekly earnings rise 3.6 pct on year.
newsitem.headline: Canada Feb weekly earnings rise 3.6 pct on year.

text.p: The preliminary estimate of average weekly earnings for Canadian workers in all industries except agriculture and fishing rose 3.6 percent in February from a year earlier to a seasonally adjusted C$598.72, Statistics Canada said on Tuesday.
From the month before, earnings rose 0.3 percent.
Seasonally adjusted payroll employment rose 0.6 percent in February to 11.16 million from an downwardly revised 11.09 million in January.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast that average weekly earnings would rise by 3.9 percent, year on year, after a 4.1 percent rise in January.
Statistics Canada also revised payroll employment numbers for January and December after discovering a significant error in processing for those months.
In January, seasonally adjusted payroll employment rose 0.2 percent to 11.09 million on the month, revised from a rise of 0.1, to 11.18 million, Statistics Canada said.
In December, it rose 0.3 percent to 11.07 million, changed from a monthly rise of 1.2 percent to 11.17 million.
"The impact of these revisions on the monthly gross domestic product and the fourth quarter labour income estimates is very small," StatsCan said.

The federal agency said it initially thought payroll numbers increased by 133,000 in December and 9,000 in January. With the corrected data, the agency now says payroll employment rose by 31,000 in December and 17,000 in January, average weekly earnings were virtually unaffected by the error, the agency said.
StatsCan warned that its methods of collecting payroll data are improving but that the data should be interpreted in the context of a long time period, especially when examining employment numbers.
The agency said its monthly labour force survey is its foremost and up-to-date source of national and provincial estimates of employment.
